extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, USPTO staff, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for USPTO examiners on restriction/election practice, search and classification standards, handling of C* classification challenges, appeals/petitions, and related prosecution steps (e.g., reissue, certificates of correction, terminal disclaimers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone restriction documentation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated the process for documenting a telephone restriction, performing a C* classification challenge if required, and incorporating the restriction into the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes clarification that a reviewing primary examiner may approve telephone restrictions by examiners without negotiation authority; examiners must document telephone restrictions and, when necessary, initiate C* classification challenges and reflect the restriction in the subsequent Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting prohibition applies to divisional inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only inventions claimed in a divisional application may potentially be subject to the prohibition against double patenting rejections under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text revised to replace 'continuing' with 'divisional' to clarify scope; applies in context of restriction/election and rejoinder analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation when making restriction requirements complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for making a restriction requirement complete by consulting with examiners who regularly examine technology when some claimed inventions are classifiable in a technology the original examiner does not examine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of the claimed inventions fall into technology areas outside the original examiner's regular examination, the examiner should consult colleagues experienced in that technology to complete a proper restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election may include patentably distinct species or groups of indistinct species
rubrics_metrics.description: Election may include designation of patentably distinct species, or of a group of patentably indistinct species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that an election of species can be a single species or a group of patentably indistinct species; procedures for preserving petition rights and for subsequent classification challenges apply equally to elections of species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious burden includes 'search and/or examination' burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated the serious burden requirement to include being a 'search and/or examination' burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether a restriction or election creates a 'serious burden', consider whether complying with the election would impose a search and/or examination burden on the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant need not point out errors if none are present
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant need not point out supposed errors if none are present (replaced 'the' with 'any').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that applicants are not required to identify errors in Office actions if there are no errors to identify; they need only challenge when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species subject to petition-preserving requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An election of species requirement is subject to the same requirements to preserve the right to petition as any other type of restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language inserted to make explicit that procedural protections and requirements for preserving petition rights apply to elections of species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species may include more than one species/group
rubrics_metrics.description: Added 'or a group of patentably indistinct species' to clarify that an election of species may potentially include more than one single species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits elections that encompass multiple related species where they are patentably indistinct; adjust processing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral election finality after Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may not disaffirm or change their election, as a matter of right, after making an oral election and receiving an Office action based upon that oral election in a pending application (cited 37 CFR 1.142(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After an oral election followed by an Office action based on that election, the applicant's election is treated as final unless specific limited procedures allow otherwise; examiners should cite 37 CFR 1.142(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit C* classification challenge after an election when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to indicate the circumstances under which the examiner should submit a C* classification challenge after an election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an election changes the classification picture or reveals potential misclassification, examiners should follow the updated criteria to determine whether to initiate a C* classification challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims ineligible for rejoinder by examiner's amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains when claims that are ineligible for rejoinder may be canceled by examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance to examiners on canceling claims that cannot be rejoined—use examiner’s amendment procedures consistent with restriction/rejoinder rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to request reconsideration treated as election without traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to request reconsideration of an election by original presentation requirement should be treated as if the election was made without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not timely request reconsideration under the original presentation requirement, treat the election as though it was made without traverse and proceed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when elected claims all found allowable after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Added a new paragraph explaining the procedure when the examiner finds all elected claims allowable following the amendment that added claims drawn to a new invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies steps to follow when amendment introduces new-invention claims and subsequently the elected claims are determined allowable; ensures proper treatment of nonelected claims and rejoin/withdrawal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-responsiveness of amendment canceling elected claims and presenting only nonelected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified the procedure for notifying the applicant that an amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention is non-responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must notify applicants that such amendments are non-responsive and explain what response is required to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction withdrawal when all nonelected claims are rejoined 'in its entirety'
rubrics_metrics.description: Added 'in its entirety' to clarify that the restriction is entirely withdrawn when all claims to the nonelected invention are rejoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When full rejoinder occurs, the prior restriction should be considered fully withdrawn; examiners should use the clarified language when documenting withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsider classification picture upon rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should reconsider whether the C* classification picture is correct upon rejoinder of a nonelected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoinder can change the classification picture; primary/regular examiners should reevaluate classification (including initiating C* challenges if warranted) before issuing further actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify 'still withdrawn' wording for nonelected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserted 'still' before 'withdrawn' to clarify that the nonelected claims were previously withdrawn and are not being rejoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise wording to avoid confusion about the status of nonelected claims in the file history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling patentably indistinct claims in copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised discussion to clarify the procedure for handling patentably indistinct claims in copending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance addresses coordination between copending files, elections, and whether claims are patentably distinct or indistinct across related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: US utility patents no longer receive USPC classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to clarify that U.S. utility patents and U.S. utility patent application publications no longer receive classifications within the U.S. Patent Classification System (USPC); USPC database for utility areas is now a static searchable database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and plant patents and plant patent publications continue to receive USPC classification; all utility patents/applications receive CPC classifications instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPC remains active for plant and design classes; Manual of Classification no longer updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Added that the USPC is a static system and no longer updated for utility classes and that 'The Manual of Classification' is no longer updated (as of Dec 31, 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should rely on CPC for utility applications and consult USPC only for design and plant where relevant; use updated intranet tools for classification resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification duties for design/plant vs. utility
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. design and plant patents and U.S. plant patent application publications receive a designated USPC classification while U.S. utility patents and U.S. utility patent application publications do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update processing and tools used depending on patent type; CPC schedules and intranet Classification Home Page are primary resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SEARCH (Web-Based Patents End-to-End Search) tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Added the Web-Based Patents End-to-End Search tool (SEARCH) as an available automated search tool for examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should use SEARCH among other automated tools when performing prior art searches as part of a thorough and complete search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must review file wrapper history and related prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must also review the file wrapper history and prior art contained in certain related applications and proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting search and examination, include related-file histories and posted prior art from copending/related proceedings (cross-references: MPEP § 904.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of variant embodiments not disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Variant embodiments which are included in the breadth or scope of a claim but not disclosed in the application may anticipate or render obvious a claim and should be considered during search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and obviousness analyses should account for claim scope that covers variants not explicitly disclosed; such variants can be relevant prior art considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to conduct a 'thorough and complete search'
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised to state that the examiners must conduct a thorough and complete search; added definitions of 'thorough and complete search.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'thorough and complete search' is defined and includes specific steps (see related rubric entries) that go beyond cursory or narrowly focused searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a thorough and complete search
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough and complete search will include the identification and review of the areas with the highest probability of including prior art and the search should cover disclosed features related to the inventive concept of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searchers must identify high-probability areas, review disclosed features tied to the inventive concept, and ensure the search covers both claimed subject matter and reasonably expected claimable features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search should cover claimed subject matter and disclosed inventive features
rubrics_metrics.description: The search should cover the claimed subject matter and should also cover the disclosed features related to the inventive concept of the claims which might reasonably be expected to be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not limit searches only to literal claim language — include disclosed embodiments and features tied to the inventive concept that could reasonably be claimed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include every pertinent CPC group/subgroup and USPC class/subclass in field of search
rubrics_metrics.description: Every group/subgroup and secondary classification area of the Cooperative Patent Classification and class/subclass of the U.S. Patent Classification pertinent to the invention should be included in the field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct search fields to cover all CPC groups/subgroups and USPC class/subclasses relevant to the invention, including secondary areas where pertinent prior art may reside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider references from each likely area where pertinent prior art exists
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough and complete search requires the consideration of references from each of the areas where the examiner is likely to find pertinent prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search strategy should span multiple technical areas and sources if the inventive concept implicates interdisciplinary or boundary-crossing prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of an application's 'classification picture'
rubrics_metrics.description: Added the definition of an application's classification picture and a new subsection discussing C* classification information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must establish and, where required, challenge the classification picture (C*), and primary examiners should review the classification picture when an application is passed to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner review of classification at issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Added a paragraph that discusses primary examiner review of the classification picture when an application is passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuance, primary examiners must confirm the classification picture is correct and that any needed C* challenges have been resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: New routing/docketing and CPC classification-challenge procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Added new sections discussing routing and docketing of applications; assignment, transfer and classification challenges under CPC; handling of new utility applications in CPC; classification and assignment of utility applications to examiners; inspection of amendments necessitating C* classification challenges; and the classification challenge procedure in CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and managers should follow newly added CPC-focused procedures for assignment, transfer, classification challenges, and routing/docketing as described in the new sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment/transfer processing for design and plant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: New sections discuss assignment and transfer of applications in USPC and classification/assignment procedures for design and plant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content moved/adapted from prior sections to reflect current design and plant application processing; follow the updated procedures for assignment and transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition acceptance guidance under 37 CFR 1.181(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised guidance to deciding officials on the acceptance of petitions filed under 37 CFR 1.181(f) filed more than 2 months from the date of the action or notice from which relief is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides consistent language for petition decisions, including matters decided by Technology Center Directors and other petition decision processes; helps deciding officials apply uniform criteria when late petitions are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure clarifications and fee handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified appellate-related procedures: Pre-Appeal Brief Review Request page limits and filing restrictions, appellant waiver of challenge implications for nonstatutory double patenting rejections, timing for appeal forwarding fee payment, and that an appellant may not request withdrawal once a properly filed notice of appeal is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes new form paragraph references (e.g., 12.278), specifics on when a Pre-Appeal Brief Review Request cannot be filed (e.g., with after-final amendments), and how mailing of examiner's answer begins certain fee time periods unless a petition is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filing and continuation timing after Federal Circuit decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants wanting to continue prosecution where all claims are rejected after a Federal Circuit decision must file a continuation application prior to the court mandate because RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 is not available in that situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural limitation affecting how to continue prosecution post-appellate decisions; examiners and applicants must follow the timing rules described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of application for allowance—procedural checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Added guidance such as determining if an extension of time is required for entry of an examiner's amendment, and cross-references to MPEP § 706.07(f); instructions for handling 'Printer Rush' and how assignee information is identified for printing on an issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should perform administrative checks before allowance/issue, ensure proper handling of examiner's amendments and assignee printing data, and follow updated cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration and 'at least one error' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that the reissue oath or declaration must specifically identify the claim and the error to support a broadening reissue and that examiners should not object if more than one error is stated; 'at least one error' is pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 251 and required by 37 CFR 1.175(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner review of reissue filings should focus on compliance with statutory/regulatory specificity requirements and updated case law citations; do not improperly restrict the number of errors stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Correction procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Added procedural details for certificates of correction: filing document descriptions for electronic filing, requirement that requests be signed and identify support in the application for Office errors, limitations on using certificates to change applicant information, and when third-party information triggers a notice of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests via electronic filing must use specific document descriptions; unsigned requests are not accepted; certificates cannot change applicant info—use 37 CFR 1.46(c) where appropriate; third-party info may prompt a notice of intent before Office acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer and eTD timing and content clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified when submitted terminal disclaimers (TD) or express terminal disclaimers (eTD) after payment of the issue fee will be accepted (unless patent face already shows language), that compliant terminal disclaimer must be filed with a reply to obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection, and requirements about common ownership at time of enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and applicants must ensure TDs/eTDs are compliant and filed timely (typically with a reply) to be effective against nonstatutory double patenting rejections; cross-reference MPEP § 804.03 for common ownership rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and double patenting withdrawal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised text to define patent term filing date and how this filing date is used to determine whether to withdraw or maintain provisional double patenting rejections in different situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess provisional double patenting rejections in light of the defined patent term filing date and applicable situations described in the revised guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing and PCT/ST.26/ST.25 incorporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised discussions to incorporate guidance from ST.25 and ST.26 rulemaking regarding sequence listings, updated PCT rule reproductions to apply to international filing dates on/after July 1, 2022, and clarified filing/formatting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use updated ST.26 guidance for sequence listings in international applications; note that tables related to sequence listings are no longer allowed in PCT international applications post-change; follow ePCT/form PCT/RO/101 filing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA/US and ISA/US procedural updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated sample International Search Report and written opinion forms, clarified protest fee policies (no protest fee under PCT Rule 40.2(e) in ISA/US; IPEA/US does not charge protest fee under PCT Rule 68.3(e)), and updated procedures for amendments under PCT Rule 66.8 and Articles 19/34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When handling PCT international search/examination matters, follow updated forms, fee policies, and amendment processing rules; include CPC classifications on PCT/IPEA/408 where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA invitations to furnish sequence listings and pay late fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA may invite the applicant to furnish a sequence listing and pay a late furnishing fee when an application contains disclosure of one or more nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences required to be included in a sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should respond to IPEA invitations promptly and follow deadlines for furnishing sequence listings to avoid procedural complications or refusal to consider sequences.
